sentences.text: In today's lesson, I want to give you some expressions that people use and that you might hear whenever you're facing a very difficult situation, or something you don't like, or something that's a little bit difficult, and the person speaking to you or the person you're
speaking with is having a hard time accepting it, and this is what some things people might say to you.
Now, some of them are, you know, just normal expressions.
Some of them are slang, so you have to be a little bit careful who you say them to and how you say them.
So, first of all, you have a bad situation.
Let's say your boss wants you to work on Saturday, but you had already made plans on Saturday.
Right?
Not a big deal, but still, you're not very happy about it, and you a little bit start to complain to your boss.
What your boss might say to you is, "Just bite the bullet and come in."
So, "bullet", like from a gun, "bite it".

So, in the old days, whenever you had an injury and they had to, like, fix it really quickly or, like, sew it up, but they didn't have the drugs to put you to sleep, they would put a bullet in your mouth, and as the pain happens, you bite on the bullet so you don't,
you know, scream or bite your tongue or whatever.
So, that's where the expression comes from.
Bite the bullet, just get through the pain, basically, is what it means.
Oh, sorry, I forgot a word here.
Take one for the team.
Take one for the team.
Take one for the team. Basically, make a sacrifice.
Even though you don't like the situation, even though you don't want to do something, you will be helping people around you.

So, make that sacrifice, accept the situation, do what needs to be done, and other people will benefit from it, and they will be happy with you, and they will like you, and hopefully, they will return the favor someday down the road.
Suck it up.
Just like that.
Just suck it up, stop complaining, start doing, it'll be over soon, and then you can go on with your life, with your day, whatever it is you want to do.
But like, a little bit harsh, a little bit rude, so be careful who you say to.
Some people will not take it very kindly.
It's a little bit slang and informal.
Same with "deal with it".
Deal with it and suck it up basically mean the same thing.
You have a problem, deal with it.
Basically means it's your problem, it's not my problem.
Don't complain to me, I don't care.
Do whatever you have to do.
If you want to quit, quit.
If you want to, you know, sacrifice somebody else, do that, but it's your problem, you deal with it, you handle it, you manage it is what it means.
Grin and bear it.
So, grin is like a fake smile basically, like just turning your lips up, but you're not really smiling because you don't really feel very happy about it.
"Bear" basically means carry it, like bear the burden.
So, just, okay, stop complaining, just grin and bear it and it'll be over very soon.
The pain will be over very soon, or the Saturday you'll finish work and you'll go out with your friends and do whatever you want.
I don't want to hear you complain, just show me your smile and just take it, deal with it.
So, get a grin and bear it.
Get a grip.
A grip is like holding on to something, that situation is a grip.
So, get a grip means stop whining.
This is actually a good word to know.
Whine, not like the drink, right, with an "h", but it sounds the same.
Sometimes people will say "whine", they'll pronounce the "h" a little bit extra, it's because it's really annoying.
So, when you're whining, you're "but I don't want to do it, I don't want to come on Saturday".
It's complaining, but like sort of a complaining and crying mixed, and people really, really don't like it.
If you do that, try to stop, because people will say all these things to you, they're not going to be very friendly about it.
So, if you're going to whine, if you're going to be complaining and crying and worrying and panicking, I'll just say just get a grip.
Just grow up, do what you have to do and move on with your life after that.
Now, these ones, these days might be a bit problematic, because you're never going to say "man up", like "be a man".
You're never going to say this to a woman, "man up".
And you're not going to say "woman up", that just doesn't - that's not an expression, so only say this to guys, basically, "man up".
Or take it like a man, basically same thing.
Be strong.
Be strong.

The idea is like a man is strong, a man can do anything, that's the idea, that's why it's a little problematic these days, because of all, you know, all kinds of political correctness, but it's still good expressions, you will hear them.
Make sure you understand what it means, just be strong is what it means.
Now, this one is a little tricky to explain.
Grow a set.
Now, a set refers to a man's parts.
The - not the long part, the other part, right?
So, "grow a pair of balls" is basically what it means, "grow a set of balls", and that means "be a man" is the essential meaning.
And "sack up", same idea, like a ball sack, so get a sack of balls and be strong, basically is what it means.
Otherwise, it's time to face the music.
So, if you have to face the music, do it.
Basically, it's similar to "deal with it".
Here's a situation, it's time to, you know, deal with it, it's time to face the music, and dance is the actual idea of the expression.
Now, what you don't want to do is throw someone under the bus.
Throw someone under the bus basically means sacrifice somebody else, right?
So, and it's usually someone who you're supposed to be friends with, or at least, you know, have a good relationship with.
So, the boss asks me to come in and work on Saturday, but I don't want to, so I say, "Oh, you know, Jimmy's actually free, I don't think he has any plans this weekend."
So, the boss will go to Jimmy and make him work.
So, what I did, I threw Jimmy under the bus, means I sacrificed him, I put him in a difficult or a bad situation, basically to save myself, and that's not something you ever want to do.
And you'll see this a lot, especially in politics.

If a politician is confronted, like a news reporter comes up to a politician and says, "Oh, you said this and this about this or this group of people", and this person says, "Oh, no, no, that wasn't me, that's my secretary.
My secretary manages my social media."
So, this person threw the secretary under the bus, because now the secretary looks bad for something that this politician did.
Not a good situation.
So, bad things happen in life.
Be prepared for people to tell you to just deal with it and, you know, grow up and get over it, basically.
Okay?
Some good expressions, be careful who you use some of them with.
